clinicalDetails.clinicalHistory: The patient was apparently normal 8 months ago when she was involved in a road traffic accident resulting in a left tibial condyle fracture and an avulsion ACL tear. Open reduction and internal fixation was performed by Dr. Hemant Kalyan, followed by 4 to 6 weeks of non-weight bearing and subsequent progressive loading. Despite 8 months having passed, the patient has not returned to full functional activity and presented for further management. Provisional diagnosis: left tibial condyle fracture status postoperative 8 months.
clinicalDetails.chiefComplaint: Left knee pain, difficulty performing functional activities and difficulty walking along with ankle and back pain during prolonged walking following surgery.

subjectiveAssessments.conclusion: Moderate pain with mild irritability particularly during prolonged walking and standing, which is relieved with rest.

tests.comments: Restricted and painful knee flexion on overpressure.
Transcript states 'knee gig 5 degrees' on the right. Restricted extension noted.
Hip range of motion was generally full and pain-free although left hip extension was restricted.
Healed surgical scar noted on the medial aspect of the knee, with swelling present.

objectiveGoals.goalName: Improve knee stability and single leg stability
Strengthen the quadriceps and functional lower limb musculature
